title: the edge-emulation base is sized for one sub-buffer and then carved into four, so the fourth runs off the end
consumer: libavcodec/diracdec.c:1898, dirac_decode_frame_internal(), against the allocation at :342
object: edge_emu_buffer_base, one av_malloc_array(stride, MAX_BLOCKSIZE) at libavcodec/diracdec.c:342
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: four sub-buffers are spaced i*FFALIGN(p->width, 16) apart inside an allocation of stride*MAX_BLOCKSIZE, while each is used for up to MAX_BLOCKSIZE rows of stride bytes -- room for one, not four
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation, no inner layer. Nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity:
real allocator, model consumer. Reduced: `width = stride = 16`, so `FFALIGN(width, 16)` is the stride and the
arithmetic is the clearest it can be; the case asserts that sub-buffer 3's last row is past the end
at the pin and inside it under the fix, so a reduction with the wrong geometry fails rather than
measuring something else. Only the FIRST crossing byte is written; `extent` records that the unreduced
path writes a whole row.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source, not from ancestry, and keyed on the IDENTIFIER rather than on the expression. Two-sided for BOTH halves of the fix: n9.0.1:libavcodec/diracdec.c contains `edge_emu_buffer_base = av_malloc_array(stride, 4 * MAX_BLOCKSIZE)` (1) and the pre-fix `...(stride, MAX_BLOCKSIZE)` form of that assignment (0), and contains `edge_emu_buffer[i] = s->edge_emu_buffer_base + i*s->buffer_stride` (1) against the pre-fix `+ i*FFALIGN` (0). A FIX-REVERSAL. NEAR-MISS RECORDED: a first probe keyed on the bare expression `av_malloc_array(stride, MAX_BLOCKSIZE)` read vuln=1 fix=1 -- NOT two-sided -- because diracdec.c:345 allocates `s->mcscratch` with the identical expression and the fix does not touch it. Keyed that way the liveness reading was ambiguous and would have gone into this file as a proof. The identifier is what makes the probe separate the two sites.
distinguishing: the only row here whose fix changes the ALLOCATION rather than an index, and the only one where there is NO inner bound to have crossed: pre-fix the four sub-buffers OVERLAP, so 'the sub-buffer's bound' is not a well-defined thing. That is what puts it in this corpus and not the sub-object one, and it is why it is filed as not-nested.

Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc020e5b8 address=0xc0251768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image 6bd768271a8f373c. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED: FAULTS at the labelled probe. The crossing leaves the allocation the platform allocator handed out, which per-object bounds enforce. NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner, as is also true of the two sibling plain-heap corpora. WHY THE PLATFORM ALLOCATOR. These cases call the platform's calloc, not the buffer-pool port's av_malloc. That port's av_malloc (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26) is a bump/freelist carve out of ONE arena returning a raw interior pointer, and it rounds every request up to 64 bytes; __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. Routing these cases through it would leave no per-allocation bound to cross AND would absorb every small crossing in the round-up, so the reading would be about the arena, not the defect.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle:
MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: **CAUGHT.** signal=34 (SIGPROT), si_code=**1** (the BOUNDS code), addr=pc=0x102120, and supervise resolved `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x102120` INDEPENDENTLY from the image -- the fault address equals the labelled probe's address, so SCHEMA rule 2 is met for this row. The crossing is 33 bytes past a 512-byte request whose capability length is exactly 512, so the crossing leaves the usable allocation. ATTRIBUTION ESTABLISHED, which no sibling plain-heap corpus can claim: this corpus defines its probes ONCE externally in shared/driver.c rather than as `static` in the header, so supervise resolves the symbol from the image independently of the run. memcached's and wireshark's rows read 'attribution: not established' precisely because their probes are static and duplicated across translation units. the capability lengths were measured IN THE SAME BOOT for this corpus's own request sizes, because the memcached/wireshark calloc table is not transferable across size classes: request 16 -> length 16 (slack 0); request 24 -> length 32 (SLACK 8); request 512 -> length 512 (slack 0); request 2048 -> length 2048 (slack 0). the platform controls fired in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY, both PASS. A first attempt at this run had both controls FAIL, because the corpus's own size probe had been passed as --abi-probe; those readings were discarded rather than reported, since a result whose platform controls did not fire is not a reading. ATTRIBUTION, restated 2026-10-06 in the form that survives a rebuild. This arm first said the fault address EQUALS the resolved probe address. That was true of the -O1 build it was measured on -- the probe compiled to essentially one instruction, so its entry WAS the faulting load -- but equality is not what attribution means and it does not survive -O0, where a frame setup puts the load ~0x10 into the function. Re-run by the committed runner (runners/run-cheribsd.sh, -O0): the fault lies INSIDE the labelled probe's extent -- ffh_read_probe spans [0x10213a, 0x102156), size 0x1c, and the fault is at 0x10214a. THAT is the criterion, and it is the one to check. The capability-length table reproduced IDENTICALLY across both builds, so the mechanism is unaffected.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 in the same vehicle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x102288, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x102270` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
